data.gender_notes: Theodelinda is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Theodelinda is derived from the Germanic elements 'Theud' meaning 'people' and 'Wald' meaning 'rule'. In Latin, it translates to 'God's gift of victory'. Theodelinda was a 6th-century queen of the Lombards, who is known for her piety and her patronage of the Roman Catholic Church. Her name is a testament to her faith and her rule over her people.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes divine guidance and victory in challenging times.
data.etymology: Theodelinda belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's gift of victory.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Theodelinda total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: תאודלינד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם תאודלינד מקורו בשפה הגרמנית, ונכנס לשפה העברית דרך הזרם הגרמני-לטיני, המייחס את השם לתאודוסיוס, 'אלוהים, ידעתי', ול-לינדה, 'אהבה', בהתאם לתפיסת העולם הנוצרית, שם זה יכול להתפרש כ'מלכת הצדק והאהבה'. בתקופה הביזנטית, תאודלינד היה שם נפוץ, והושווה לתאודורה, 'מלכה של אלוהים'.

in_greek.name: Θεοδολίνδη
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όνομα Θεοδολίνδη προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα και εισήλθε στην ελληνική γλώσσα μέσω του γερμανικού-λατινικού ρεύματος, το οποίο συνδέει το όνομα με τον Θεόδωσο, 'Εγώ γνωρίζω τον Θεό', και την Λίνδη, 'Αγάπη', σύμφωνα με την ερμηνεία του Χριστιανισμού. Στον Χριστιανισμό, το όνομα Θεοδολίνδη μπορεί να μεταφραστεί ως 'Βασιλομήτωρ δικαιοσύνη και ἀγάπη'.

in_latin.name: Theodelinda
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Theodelinda originem habet ex lingua Germanica et introductum est in linguam Latinam per fluxum Germano-Latinum, qui nomen coniungit cum Theodosio, 'Ego scio Deum', et Lindae, 'Amor', secundum intellectum Christianitatis. In Christianismo, nomen Theodelinda potest interpretari ut 'Regina iustitia et amor'.

in_english.name: Theodelinda
in_english.long_meaning: The name Theodelinda originates from the German language and entered the Latin language through the Germano-Latin current, which connects the name to Theodosius, 'I know God', and Linda, 'Love', in accordance with the Christian understanding. In Christianity, the name Theodelinda can be interpreted as 'Queen of justice and love'.

data.cultural_impact: Theodelinda's name reflects her influential role as a queen and her connection to the Germanic and Christian traditions. She was the first Christian ruler of the Lombards and her court became a center of artistic and cultural production. The name "Theodelinda" remains an important part of European history and a reminder of the political and cultural interplay between the Germanic and Roman worlds during the Middle Ages.
data.spiritual_significance: Theodelinda's name reflects her deep faith and her role as a patron of the Roman Catholic Church. She was known for her devotion and her support for the spread of Christianity among her people. Her name 'God's gift of victory' highlights the belief that her rule and her faith were divinely inspired and ordained. She is a model of piety and leadership, demonstrating the power of faith to inspire and guide ruling leaders in difficult times.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Theodelinda: Divine gift of a brave, tender-hearted woman. Grace and valor embodied.

historical_references.reference: Theodelinda was the last ruling member of the Lombard dynasty in Italy. She is known for her conversion to Catholicism and her patronage of the arts.
historical_references.context: Theodelinda ruled as Queen of the Lombards from 612-628 AD. She converted from Arianism, a form of Christianity that did not acknowledge the divinity of Jesus, to Catholicism, solidifying the Catholic Church's position in Italy.

historical_references.reference: Theodelinda's reign marked the beginning of the early medieval period in Italy, and her patronage of the arts contributed to the establishment of a distinct Italian style in art and architecture.
historical_references.context: Theodelinda's reign saw the development of the early medieval period in Italy, characterized by the emergence of distinct Italian styles in art and architecture. Her patronage of the arts, which included the construction of several churches, contributed to this cultural shift.

modern_usage.modern_context: Theodelinda (c. 570-628 AD) was a powerful and influential queen of the Lombards, ruling from 612 to 628 AD. She is remembered for her significant contributions to the spread of Christianity in northern Italy, as well as her patronage of the arts and architecture. In academic and scholarly contexts, Theodelinda is studied as a pivotal figure in European history and the development of the Roman Catholic Church. In the Catholic Church, she is venerated as a saint and her relics are preserved in various churches throughout Italy. In museums and exhibitions, Theodelinda's life and legacy are showcased as an example of female leadership and the role of women in medieval Europe.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Ruth Theodelinda in Rome, Italy credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Theodelinda, which means "God's gift of victory". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
